name: Inngest
description: Event-driven background job and workflow SDK for TypeScript-first teams. Runs as serverless functions triggered by events or schedules, with built-in retry logic and execution history. The simpler alternative to Trigger.dev for teams that need durable background execution without self-hosting infrastructure.

ecosystem_fit.notes: Used in Base AI agent workflows for event-driven background job execution triggered by Alchemy webhooks.
Works with Ethereum event pipelines via Alchemy or QuickNode webhooks.
Neynar webhooks can trigger Inngest functions for Farcaster agent workflows.
Can be used with Helius webhooks but Trigger.dev has stronger Solana agent adoption.

common_pairings.context: Inngest manages the job lifecycle (trigger, retry, logging); Vercel AI SDK handles the LLM reasoning within each Inngest step.
Alchemy address-activity webhooks trigger Inngest functions for EVM event-driven agent workflows on Base and Ethereum.
Neynar webhooks fire Inngest functions when Farcaster events occur, enabling durable social agent response workflows.
Inngest and Trigger.dev serve the same orchestration role. Inngest is simpler to onboard; Trigger.dev provides more powerful durable execution for complex long-running agents.

trust_evidence.description: Inngest v3 is actively maintained with frequent releases. Well-documented Next.js and Node.js integrations.
Widely used in TypeScript-first application teams for background job orchestration. Cited as an alternative to Trigger.dev in Solana and Base agent workflow discussions.

scale_guidance.hackathon: Skip orchestration at hackathon scale. Inngest is worth adding from MVP onward for any app with background jobs.
scale_guidance.mvp: Inngest's free tier and Next.js integration make it the lowest-friction way to add background job execution. Add it as soon as you have agent workflows that need retry logic.
scale_guidance.production: Configure concurrency limits before scaling. Inngest's execution history is essential for debugging agent failures in production. Plan for Inngest cloud pricing at high job volumes.

alternatives.when_to_prefer: When you need durable execution with fine-grained step visibility, complex long-running workflows, or strong Solana agent adoption patterns. Trigger.dev has more powerful retry and observability for complex agents.
alternatives.ecosystem_context: All chains — especially Solana where Trigger.dev adoption is stronger.

alternatives.when_to_prefer: When workflows require very long-running durability (hours to days) with strong consistency guarantees. Temporal has significantly higher operational complexity.

anti_patterns: Using Inngest for very long-running workflows (>10 min steps) — Trigger.dev's durable execution model handles these better.
Skipping concurrency limits — Inngest functions without concurrency controls will spin up unbounded parallel executions under high webhook load.
Running Inngest in production without execution history review — the execution logs are the primary debugging tool; ignoring them means agent failures go undetected.
